label: heart-s1-c1

analysis.note: Train split only, full sample (n=242); local forward passes on in-memory copies. Linear replacement = each hidden ReLU replaced by its least-squares affine fit on its pre-activation; restore gain = AUC gain from putting one ReLU back onto the all-linearised model.

resisted: Nothing resisted coverage; only input fan-out needed splitting (ca x3, slope:2, thalach). Four of seven hidden ReLUs (664, 1173, 2245, 2650) never clip on train, so their annotations describe affine relays (reweighting of ca, slope:2, cp:3 and the heart-rate hinge) rather than distinct concepts. 3210 is a pure cp:1 switch (on for all 22 typical-angina patients, off for the rest), so its best linear fit is almost exact. Nine unconnected inputs (sex:1, fbs:0, restecg:1, restecg:2, exang:0, exang:1, slope:1, thal:4, thal:7) listed as zero-effect root entries.
tool_bugs: Root annotation via apply_operation must exclude child subgraph nodes (passing the whole graph is refused as 'already covered'); not a bug, but undocumented in the protocol. Otherwise none observed with v3 tooling.
summary: Essentially logistic regression (all hidden units linearised: train AUC 0.9355 vs 0.9392; L2 logistic regression 0.9355). 13 direct edges carry logit SD 4.25 of 5.63; ca enters by three parallel routes (effective +2.60 logit per SD), cp:3 only via always-on relay 1173. The one consequential nonlinearity is gate 1801 = ReLU(1.54 restecg:0 + 0.82 oldpeak - 1.52): ST depression adds risk only with a normal resting ECG (+0.0034 AUC over linear). Typical angina (cp:1) lowers risk via switch 3210, less with more vessels; a small hinge lets higher max heart rate lower risk. Same design as the 10-seed heart-s1 record (gen-31 genome), with an added typical-angina switch and heart-rate hinge.
